summary: This article explains why children need nine to twelve hours of sleep, how light from screens confuses the body's inner clock and melatonin, and what bedtime habits help everyone sleep better.
introduce: Draw a simple cause → effect arrow on the board and ask students for an everyday example, such as “I did not sleep, so I felt tired.” Tell them that while reading “Sleep and Screens” they will find at least two cause-and-effect links.

keyTerms.def: a chemical the brain makes when it gets dark that helps you feel sleepy
wide awake and paying close attention
a set of actions you do in the same order every day

challengeTerms.def: following a daily cycle of about twenty-four hours, like the body's sleep and wake pattern
a chemical made by the body that carries messages in the blood to control things like growth and sleep
to give all your attention to one thing

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that using a phone or tablet in bed is fine as long as you turn it off before you fall asleep? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Your friend says, "Sleep is just wasted time." Write a reply that uses at least two facts from the article to change your friend's mind.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review melatonin, alert, and routine, and let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use circadian, hormone, and concentrate in a short paragraph that explains one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
